newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar to record close on Dow, rates.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar to record close on Dow, rates.

text.p: Mexican stocks resumed their New Year rally on Tuesday with their sixth record close in seven trading sessions, which traders and analysts said was fueled by a bullish Dow Jones and forecasts of further falls in domestic interest rates.
"People really got fired up today. We were snowed under by orders (to buy)," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index closed up 69.18 points, or 1.96 percent, at 3,631.36. Volume was heavy at 125.3 million shares traded.
Analysts expected a bout of profit-taking on Monday to spill over into Tuesday's session, but last week's rally resumed after foreign buyers swamped the market.

"It has to be said the market is being valued more suitably. We feel the main reason is foreign funds rejigging portfolios in favor of Latin American markets, particularly in Brazil and Mexico," said Roberto Garcia, investment adviser at the Vector brokerage.
Garcia added the bourse gained on forecast falls in primary rates and sharp gains in share prices on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones closed up 0.79 percent at 6,762.29 points.

A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed they saw bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) rates assigned at an average of 23.75 percent at the primary auction later in the day, a fall of 49 basis points since last week.
A technical analyst said the rally may take a breather before continuing.

"Although we will head towards new highs at 3,650 points, it would be best to consolidate again in order to avoid a greater (downward) adjustment," said Hector Jimenez, an analyst with the Inverlat financial group.
On the broad market, a greater-then-usual total of 125 stocks were traded, of which gains trounced losses by 65 to 32.
Traders said most stocks at the head of the gainers' list were not blue chips, but stragglers left behind by the recent rally and thus attractively priced.
Chemical manufacturer Cydsasa was one heavily traded winner, ending up 1.44 pesos at 16.84 pesos.
Another leader in percentage terms was mining firm Penoles, up 1.40 pesos to 28.40, following an upgrade to buy from sell by Kleinwort Benson.
